notes.title: Ecliptica: PreDemo 1.4
notes.content: [p]Hello, Ecliptica community![/p][p]We're incredibly excited to announce that we've finally reached the point where we can let you get a taste of our game. This isn't the final version, but rather a "raw" sample of what awaits us in the future. The goal of these playtests is to let you see the look of our game and also check how it performs on your hardware.[/p][p]Please note: this update includes only 1/16 of the planned content. It features just one, still very rough, construction mechanic, and lacks full gameplay.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]How to Participate?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]A detailed guide on how to launch and play the demo can be found here: [url="https://ecliptica.fandom.com/wiki/How_to_play"]https://ecliptica.fandom.com/wiki/How_to_play[/url][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]Changelog – What's New and What's Been Done[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We've combined all our previous internal developments so you can see the full journey we've taken and all the key innovations available in the current version.[/p][list][*][p]Added a [b]trading[/b] mechanic and new items (protein-carbon bar, purified metals, ore, and construction blueprints).[/p][/*][*][p]Implemented a [b]seamless and infinite world[/b] mechanic that no longer relies on chunks.[/p][/*][*][p]Added [b]new biomes[/b]: Plains, Forests, and Highlands. The forests are now divided into sub-biomes by height, and the Plains have been completely reworked.[/p][/*][*][p]Significantly [b]reworked graphics and performance[/b]: improved shader visualization, completely redone shadows, and increased render distance to 15 km.[/p][/*][*][p]Added [b]graphics and sound settings[/b], as well as the main menu and in-game audio.[/p][/*][*][p]Added the [b]first mob[/b] — the Resident (colony inhabitant).[/p][/*][*][p]Implemented an [b]in-game physics system[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Added the ability to [b]destroy and change the world[/b], along with many other improvements.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]New Trailer![/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We're also presenting you with an updated game trailer so you can see all the visual changes.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="ASwHlP7EkU4;full"][/previewyoutube][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]We're Looking Forward to Your Feedback[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Your feedback and bug reports are invaluable to us. Yes, we know there are a lot of bugs... and we're really hoping for your help in finding them![/p][p]Thank you for your support![/p]

notes.title: Ecliptica Devlog #10 Interactive World
notes.content: [h3][b]Hello, friends![/b] [/h3][p]We're incredibly excited to share our tenth dev diary with you. In this video, we're showing off some new features that we've been working on. And with that, let's go![/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][previewyoutube="cBZpczFAvJI;full"][/previewyoutube][h3][b]Dynamic and destructible world [/b][/h3][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45621583/ad3a36090f3c1abfdb4bbe6df0dd45ec957c7744.jpg"][/img][/p][p]One of the [b]biggest new features[/b] you'll see in this dev diary is a [b]fully interactive and destructible world[/b]. We're showing how players will be able to [b]destroy landscape elements[/b] such as [b]large boulders, trees, grass[/b] — [b]basically everything in the game[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]Landscape deformation[/b] [/h3][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45621583/ef1a42f302a77720d87a2a0e0a7fcf2d7f85860e.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Our world[/b] is not only destructible, but also [b]subject to change[/b]. You can [b]dig, build, and pile up[/b], which makes the [b]landscape player-controllable[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Support for Rigging, Morphing, and other Qt Quick 3D features[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45621583/4201352ac862362c6ed4bd42d54d701dbbb6f9f2.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Finally, we've gotten to integrating Qt Quick 3D's game features[/b] such as the [b]particle system, rigging, and morphing animation[/b]. These are quite [b]basic functions in game development[/b], and without them, the game would have looked bland. [b]But now you don't have to worry about that anymore![/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Landscape blueprint system[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45621583/a7c6e358b5616924c7a40ad38497f7541e3fb716.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We are constantly thinking about how to give you more creative freedom. That's why we have developed a new [b]landscape blueprint system[/b]. This [b]intuitive interface[/b] will allow you to [b]create and save your own landscape designs[/b]. You will be able to [b]plan, modify, and save terrain changes[/b] to easily return to your favorite creations or [b]share them with others[/b]. What's more, in the game, [b]every blueprint is essentially commercial property that can be sold![/b][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]Next steps[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We continue to [b]work hard on Ecliptica[/b] and thank you for your [b]support and interest[/b]. Your [b]feedback is very important to us[/b]. Be sure to [b]check out the full video[/b].[/p][p][b]Watch the full Devlog 10 here:[/b][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/cBZpczFAvJI"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][b]Thanks for following our project! Don't forget to leave your comments and ask questions.[/b][/p]

notes.title: Ecliptica Devlog #9: A Visual Transformation of the World
notes.content: [p][/p][h1][b]Hello, survivors![/b][/h1][p][/p][p]We're excited to present our new devlog! This time, we focused on making the world of [b]Ecliptica[/b] even more alive and [b]beautiful[/b].[/p][p]We've completely updated the [b]jungle graphics[/b]. Now there are new plants, more realistic shadows, and, the coolest part, trees now sway in the wind. This adds an incredible atmosphere to the game world.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/0385252b5f46ca18f88d5a5c5a65c1f61fe1bbbe.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We also worked on the [b]drawing distance[/b]. The horizon no longer looks blurry, and distant objects are now much more detailed. This will help you get even more immersed in the game's atmosphere.[/p][p][/p][p]We hope you like these changes. And that's not all! We're continuing to work hard, and in the next devlog, we'll show you other things we're currently working on.[/p][p]Don't forget to add [b]Ecliptica[/b] to your wishlist so you don't miss our next announcements![/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="NMLR_q2Ukb0;full"][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Multiplayer in Ecliptica: Our Plans for Co-op Play!
notes.content: [p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/1e44adba2f322f7662af59af377d5f0ae6e92782.png"][/img][/p][p]Hello everyone![/p][hr][/hr][p]Today, I want to talk about our plans for launching [b]multiplayer[/b] in Ecliptica. It's no secret that survival games are most fun when played with friends. And while Ecliptica isn't a classic survival game, playing with friends is always more enjoyable![/p][p]We plan to implement multiplayer for small groups, up to [b]10 people[/b]. This feature is scheduled for the [b]Alpha version[/b] of the game. It won't be in the upcoming [b]Demo[/b] release; that will be single-player only.[/p][p]Game development will be divided into chapters, with each chapter including both major and regular updates.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3]Our Approximate Game Development Roadmap:[/h3][p][/p][list][*][p][b]0. Pre-Demo:[/b] This is essentially the preparatory stage we are currently in. We might conduct playtests for anyone interested here before the demo release.[/p][/*][*][p][b]1. Demo:[/b] Here we will showcase the basic game mechanics and, of course, Ecliptica's open and infinite world. This build will be available for free to all users as an introductory version of the game.[/p][/*][*][p][b]2. Alpha:[/b] This will be the first paid version of the game, available in Early Access. Multiplayer will be integrated at this stage.[/p][/*][*][p][b]3. Beta:[/b] At this stage, we plan to actively expand the world and its mechanics. We won't reveal too many details yet; you'll learn more as we progress.[/p][/*][*][p][b]4. Release:[/b] This stage will mark the game's exit from Early Access. The goal is to expand the game's accessibility, introduce new platforms, and so on. More details will follow as we approach this stage.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]So, for now, there's one clear piece of news: we have definitively decided that multiplayer will be included, and we are starting its implementation![/p][p]Stay tuned for the latest updates![/p]

notes.title: Ecliptica pre alpha release teaser
notes.content: [p][/p][previewyoutube="MtVmoGXsACA;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Welcome to the procedurally generated, dense, infinitely vast, and [b]stylized[/b] world of [b]Ecliptica[/b].[/p][p]You are one of the colonists on an alien planet, fighting for the survival of both your colony and yourself. In this world, you can:[/p][list][*][p][b]Mine:[/b] All resources in the game are extracted, processed, and created in your colony's factories; nothing appears out of nowhere.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Trade:[/b] All prices for all goods are regulated solely by a free market, without any restrictions – whether it's food or high-tech power cells.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Manage:[/b] Every worker wants to become a manager: more power means more money. But if that's not enough, you can create your own corporation and bring the entire colony under your control.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Ecliptica Game Development log 8
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/fc2109c89ffd2ab173f709eef2b76bbad7ff6706.png"][/img]
Hello everyone! We've reached a moment to share our progress. Since [b]Developer Journal 7[/b], we've accomplished a lot, and today you can finally see the impact of our new vertex adaptation system.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Infinite World with Massive View Distance[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks to this new system, we've managed to create a truly [b]infinite open world[/b]! The map is no longer limited by a pre-generated, fixed area as it was before. Now, the world of Ecliptica is endless, just like in Minecraft, and it boasts an incredibly large [b]view distance of 20 kilometers in diameter[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]New Biomes and Improved Shading[/p][p][/p][p]We've also added a new biome to the game: the [b]Plains[/b], and we've significantly [b]improved the game's shading[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Convenient Construction[/p][p][/p][p]Furthermore, we've introduced a player-friendly [b]building construction mode[/b]. Now, you can not only focus on building your business but also an entire city! Though, one doesn't stop the other.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="wxPwA2-JBLM;full"][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Ecliptica Game Development log 7
notes.content:
[p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/905b504a740a256691b8493a8d314411c2ce6898.png"][/img][/p][p]Hello everyone![/p][p]The time has come to share one of our most important achievements to date. Although this is a purely [b]technical advancement[/b], which will likely be of most interest to other Qt developers, it will also [b]affect all players[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][h3]From the Old System to the New: Why We Changed?[/h3][p]Previously, like most developers, we used a [b]tile-based LOD system[/b] for generating the game world. Essentially, we created chunks based on heightmaps using Qt HeightFieldGeometry. This solution worked initially, but over time, our ambitions for draw distance grew. When we added rocky and sandy terrains to the game, we encountered many problems:[/p][list][*][p][b]Grid around tiles:[/b] Unsightly lines separating parts of the world.[/p][/*][*][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/1c0ef60a43b1d3efa44ca064ea1369905abc0256.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][b]Increased CPU load:[/b] The number of tiles reached up to 1600, heavily stressing the system.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Difficulties with smoothing transitions:[/b] When players changed altitudes (e.g., during resource extraction), transitions looked unpolished.[/p][/*][/list][p]These problems were very difficult to solve.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]Inspiration from UE5 and Our Solution[/h3][p]In the process of finding solutions, we came across the terrain implementation in UE5, specifically their [b]Nanite[/b] system. This impressed us greatly, and we decided to create an analogous system in Qt.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]The Result: A More Detailed and Lighter World[/h3][p]Unlike UE5, our system currently works [b]only for primitives[/b] (e.g., ocean or ground), but it has [b]completely solved all our problems![/b] Now we can create [b]much more detailed terrain[/b] that is [b]significantly less demanding on gaming hardware[/b].

[/p][previewyoutube="Kva9UvD_kng;full"][/previewyoutube][p]We are very excited about these changes and believe they will make the game world even better and more performant for each of you!

[dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/Kva9UvD_kng"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Development logs 0 - 6
notes.content:
These are all the missed development logs since we started publishing.

[h2]Developing Log 0[/h2]

  We chose a first platform to publish super early access for our game. And although our main goal is to publish on Steam, while the game is still very raw, we will be posting builds on the itch.io platform, so that everyone who is interested in whether it is possible to write a full-fledged big game with an OpenWorld system on the Qt Quick 3D engine could feel for themselves how and what is obtained in this experiment.

  Spoiler: Yes, it is possible!


[h2]Development log 1[/h2]


  As you know, we chose a not-so-easy way to implement our product; we chose the Qt Quick 3D engine as our main development tool. And of course, a few screenshots of what the early version of the game will look like.

  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/3a5f816bcd3409a65b3b7503ec8d1b33e1757e1b.gif[/img]
  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/12d86827f2e9a315b4807e9f365e74df7780e52f.png[/img]
  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/03f2557932805b8aabc22e9700252015b3b68736.jpg[/img]
  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45621583/53579d1fb94f5c2938e11c1f9e3d4329cb89853a.png[/img]


  [b]And now the most interesting part - What we did last week.[/b]

  [*] Prepared new assets for our 2 starting biomes in the game.
  [*] Added a function for distant drawing of our world.
  [*] Added wind to our world.
  [*] And probably my favorite) - Added basic functions to our corporation management mechanics in the game.

  Of course, we still have a lot to do, and soon we will organize platforms for collecting funds for development. So that we have more opportunities to prepare as full an early version of the game as possible.

  I also want to note that we are not going to compete with developers who make games on Unity or Unreal Engine, (P.S. in terms of beauty and rendering, these guys will definitely beat us no matter how hard we try), our goal is to make the game exciting and enjoyable to explore. We chose Qt so that the final product would be truly unique and interesting to people. Since we will not have tempting opportunities to throw ready-made typical mechanics into the game.


[h2]Development log 2[/h2]

  [b]What we did last week:[/b]

  [*] Basic trading mechanics. - we want to create a completely free economy in the game. Everything must be mined, prepared, and used. Of course, the economy cannot work without trading.
  [*] Improve the AI ​​of the colony inhabitants. This is a really important task, because only the inhabitants can make our economic system so alive.
  [*] Improve the visualization of some scenes
  [*] Added the ocean biome

  [previewyoutube=JP1XBWMKGok;full][/previewyoutube]


[h2]Development log 3[/h2]


  [b]Manager[/b] - this is the most popular job in the new colony among all residents… And apparently, a certain Anthony Takahash has already rushed to get a job in Capital Town - it seems to be the most prestigious job in the initial stages of the game - after all, that's where all the starting goods necessary for survival in the game are sold. And it seems that our new cunning manager has already noticed that the demand is simply huge, and the first thing he did was raise the prices for food. The player can also get this job - if they have time, of course)
  [b]Residents[/b] - Residents are the main inhabitants of the new city; in fact, they are the main characters of our game. They have needs and ambitions, and based on this, they try to find their place in the economy of our game.
  Significant improvements to open-world generation, and although there is still a lot of work to do in this segment, we have managed to diversify locations even within a single biome. You can see how it looks now.
  Updated the contents of the Forest biome
  [b]Let’s go for a walk in our new world with our new dev log video!!![/b]

  [previewyoutube=qE5EPXbGub8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Development log 4[/h2]

  [b]What is the City in the Ecliptica world?[/b] The City is a place where everyone can find food, a job, and a home.
  The city is run by corporations; corporations own property for which residents work. Each resident decides for themselves who to work with and what activity to engage in.
  Also, each of them can found a new corporation if they accumulate enough money.

  [b]City[/b] - this is just a place…
  [b]Construction[/b] - is a process that requires significant investment, and it also creates economic entities that, in turn, open up opportunities for residents.
  [b]Free pricing[/b] - you and other game participants can set any prices for your goods - but it is worth remembering that there are competitors who will happily bankrupt a greedy businessman)

  [previewyoutube=BK58mtR4vxw;full][/previewyoutube]


[h2]Development log 5[/h2]


  The week is coming to an end, and it’s time to share what is perhaps our most notable achievement lately.
  We’ve significantly optimized the game and increased the effective render distance to 1700 meters from the player — which is more than what most games with procedurally generated worlds offer.

  💡 Effective render distance means not just terrain visibility, but also full rendering of vegetation and other decorative game elements that bring the world to life.
  Additionally, thanks to Qt Instancing, we were able to greatly increase the number of objects in the scene without compromising performance.

  The current build can now handle 10,000 to 20,000 objects simultaneously without major issues.
  Of course, this parameter will be included in the settings, so players can adjust it to suit their system’s capabilities.
  Stay tuned — more improvements coming soon!

  [previewyoutube=NzL_VFDRxps;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Development log 6[/h2]

  [b]Developer Log 6[/b]
  This is the sixth entry in our development log.

  In this update, we’re introducing new buildings and the terminal system.
  [b]Buildings[/b]
  Buildings are standard in-game objects that perform various functions:

    [*] they can produce resources, act as local marketplaces, or serve other gameplay roles.

  Each building is an interactive element and plays a key part in the game’s economy and structure.
  [b]Terminals[/b]
  All buildings are equipped with terminals — interfaces that allow the player to interact with them.

  Through terminals, players can control production, manage storage, or initiate building-specific actions.
  More functional and visual improvements are in progress.

  [previewyoutube=oYy4yc-_GHc;full][/previewyoutube]
